title: 1939 Brighton Audax crash
summary: A Hawker Audax aircraft en route from Gatwick to RAF Tangmere encountered dense fog and the pilot became lost in the low visibility. Flying very low while seeking landmarks, he avoided descending on a group of Wolf Cub Scouts by continuing flight. The aircraft struck a greenhouse, shed, tree, and radio antenna before crashing into the outer wall and kitchen of a house in Brighton's Hanover area.
probable_cause: Pilot spatial disorientation in dense fog leading to inappropriate low-altitude flying in populated area and inability to land safely.

factors.evidence: pilot became lost in low visibility and was far off course
pilot was unable to identify local landmarks
pilot flew very low within 50 ft of safety seeking landing place
aircraft crashed into outer wall of house on Freshfield Road

events.text: Aircraft en route from Gatwick to RAF Tangmere encountered dense fog
Pilot became lost in low visibility and was far off course
Pilot flew very low over Whitehawk Hill within 50 ft of safety seeking landing place but saw Wolf Cub Scouts and continued flying
Aircraft struck greenhouse, shed, tree and radio antenna mast
Aircraft crashed into outer wall and kitchen of house on Freshfield Road, fuel tank exploded

notes: Military training aircraft, pilot was sole crew member

title: Japan Airways Kuma-go crash
summary: Japan Airways Kuma-go, a Lockheed L-14 Super Electra, crashed at Gannos Airport on 1939-05-17 with 6 fatalities and 5 injured.

events.text: Japan Airways Kuma-go crashed at Gannos Airport

title: 1939 Pan Am Sikorsky S-43 crash
summary: The Sikorsky S-43B Baby Clipper crashed in Guanabara Bay near Rio de Janeiro on approach after the left engine lost power. As the aircraft descended in a left yaw turn, the pitch angle steepened and the aircraft struck a caisson and crashed into the bay. Fourteen of sixteen on board were killed; two passengers survived.
probable_cause: Loss of power on the left engine during approach, resulting in descending left yaw turn with increasing pitch angle, causing collision with obstruction and water impact.

factors.evidence: As the aircraft was circling Rio in preparation for approach, the left engine lost power
The loss of power put the aircraft into a descending left yaw turn; as the yaw grew sharper, the pitch angle also steepened
The aircraft struck a caisson and crashed into Guanabara Bay, about 1 km from Santos Dumont Airport

events.text: Aircraft neared Rio de Janeiro destination and circled in preparation for normal approach
Left engine lost power during the circling maneuver
Aircraft entered descending left yaw turn with increasingly steep pitch angle
Aircraft struck caisson and crashed into Guanabara Bay about 1 kilometer from Santos Dumont Airport

notes: Limited technical details on engine failure cause or crew response; text provides narrative but minimal investigation findings
